clue.text: Stuff and nonsense, sweet!

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned exclamation of contempt for rubbish talk, like 'Bosh!'
a soft confection of sugar, butter and milk

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a remark as rubbish while praising a sweet treat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an exclamation brushing aside nonsense and the name of a soft, crumbly confection.

clue.text: On the railway, if not in the dining-car

definitions.text: On the railway, if not in the dining-car

parts.words: On the railway, if not in the dining-car
parts.note: a dish for serving fish belongs in the dining car, but on the track the same name is the bar bolted across a rail joint

explanation.surface: Something found on a train journey, though not where meals are served.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal bar joining two rail ends shares its name with a serving dish for fish.

clue.text: Object to being not quite sober

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means sober, modest and reserved

explanation.surface: A complaint about being called slightly tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite sober' reads as drunk; it means DEMURE with its last letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: It's no way to be put out

definitions.text: It's no way to be put out

parts.words: It's no way to be put out
parts.note: a way in is no way out; and to be put into a trance is to be put out

explanation.surface: A protest that one should not be inconvenienced like this.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun it is a way in, not out; as a verb (stress on the second syllable) it means to put into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is a way in, never out; the verb means to hypnotise or delight.

clue.text: Where " Charity begins at home "

parts.note: the proverb is read literally: a house provided by charity for the poor, so charity begins at that home

explanation.surface: A question about where the old proverb about charity starting at home applies.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a house was a dwelling founded by a benefactor where the aged poor lived free, so it was a home run on charity.

clue.text: A regular mystery enshrouds 'the host

annotationWithheld.why: A regular mystery enshrouds the host (4): ARMY is the host, but no parse of 'A regular mystery enshrouds' gives the letters with each word doing one job

clue.text: Prey to Bishop Wilberforce's Timbuctoo cassowary

definitions.text: Prey to Bishop Wilberforce's Timbuctoo cassowary

parts.words: Prey to Bishop Wilberforce's Timbuctoo cassowary
parts.note: the comic verse attributed to Samuel Wilberforce has a cassowary in Timbuctoo eating a churchman sent abroad, hymn-book too

explanation.surface: A reference to the victim in a Victorian bishop's nonsense rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme goes: 'If I were a cassowary / On the plains of Timbuctoo, / I would eat a ...', with cassock, bands and hymn-book too.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's victim is a churchman sent to spread the faith abroad.

clue.text: A brave man to get in on the drug scene

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bold figure getting involved in the narcotics world.
explanation.definitionFit: An addictive opiate derived from morphine.

clue.text: Singular confidence in the stock market?

definitions.text: Singular confidence in the stock market?

parts.words: Singular confidence in the stock market?
parts.note: read as single (one) plus faith, it describes a pooled investment fund

explanation.surface: An investor's remarkable faith in shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like 'remarkable'; it means one, a single thing, and 'confidence' is faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund that pools investors' money in shares, split into units, is managed by trustees.

clue.text: Clear sky round the east, right?

indicators.note: round signals turning these letters about into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone checks that the sky to the east is cloudless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges THE and E into ETHE, and R for 'right' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the clear upper air or heavens.

clue.text: Now and then I seem most upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits that occasionally they look extremely troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like it describes the speaker, but it tells you to rearrange I SEEM MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally, from time to time, is the meaning of both phrases.

clue.text: This stag burnt in 1933, in Germany

definitions.text: This stag burnt in 1933, in Germany

parts.words: This stag burnt in 1933, in Germany
parts.note: the German parliament building burnt in 1933 was the ...; the word wanted is the part standing for 'This' in front of 'stag'

explanation.surface: A remark about a deer that was burnt in Germany in 1933.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1933 fire that the Nazis used to seize power gutted the German parliament building; split its name and 'stag' is the second half, so 'This' is the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for empire, as in the Third Reich, which this clue reaches by splitting the parliament building's name.

clue.text: In which views of women are out of order

definitions.text: In which views of women are out of order

parts.words: In which views of women are out of order
parts.note: read literally: a custom of seclusion under which looking at women is not permitted, rather than one where opinions of them are improper

explanation.surface: A complaint about a setting where attitudes to women are unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' sounds like a modern objection to sexist opinions; here it means that seeing women is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The custom in parts of South Asia of screening women from the sight of men outside the family.

clue.text: Such evil omens can't be right

definitions.text: Such evil omens can't be right

parts.words: Such evil omens can't be right
parts.note: ill-boding signs are described by a word that in heraldry also means left-hand, so they literally cannot be on the right

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to believe that a run of bad portents is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin for left-hand came to mean threatening or ill-omened, so the word covers both the evil omens and the left side.

clue.text: 21 said to involve dexterity

indicators.note: to involve suggests tangling, as in involved meaning intricate, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the answer to 21 down, a muscle that stretches a body part

explanation.surface: A muscle reportedly needs skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Look up 21 down first; its six letters joined with SAID are tangled by 'to involve'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill with the hands or mind, nimbleness.

clue.text: Prior must have a follower -

parts.note: something earlier in time is only so called if something comes after it, as a grammatical referent precedes its pronoun

explanation.surface: A rule that the head of a monastery needs a disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' reads as the monastery official; it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going before; in logic and grammar it is paired with what follows it.

clue.text: Standard maintained in France

parts.note: a standard is a flag, and the French one has three colours

explanation.surface: A level of quality upheld by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French national flag of blue, white and red bands is a flag, which is a standard.

clue.text: Depression, or its opposite

definitions.meaning: in British slang, having the sulks or a fit of low spirits
a raised lump or mound, the reverse of a hollow

explanation.surface: Someone notes a dip in the ground, or perhaps a bump.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'to have the hump' is to be in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bout of low spirits and a raised mound, the reverse of a hollow.

clue.text: They go 'from equator to poles in ever-decreasing circles

definitions.text: They go 'from equator to poles in ever-decreasing circles

parts.words: They go 'from equator to poles in ever-decreasing circles
parts.note: the lines of latitude are circles that shrink as they approach the poles

explanation.surface: People going round and round, achieving less and less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ever-decreasing circles' is an idiom for futile activity; here it is literal geography.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of latitude are circles on the globe that get smaller towards the poles.

clue.text: In Dickens he's no relation to Susan Nipper

definitions.text: In Dickens he's no relation to Susan Nipper

parts.words: In Dickens he's no relation to Susan Nipper
parts.note: a nip and a pinch are the same thing, yet the Martin Chuzzlewit character is unrelated to Dombey and Son's maid

explanation.surface: A note that two Dickens characters are not family.
explanation.walkthrough: Susan Nipper is the maid in Dombey and Son; the gentle organist in Martin Chuzzlewit has a surname meaning a nip.
explanation.definitionFit: The kindly organist in Martin Chuzzlewit whose surname means a nip, linking him to Nipper.

clue.text: Quick come-back? That's not good

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the reverse direction, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: quick in its old sense means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'

explanation.surface: A question about a speedy retort, judged to be poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' in the archaic sense of living; 'come-back' turns LIVE round.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or wrong is the opposite of good.

clue.text: Place of our quiet rest? Could be

definitions.text: Place of our quiet rest? Could be

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters before may be rearranged into something else

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: A wistful question about where we lie in peace, perhaps a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a grave; the anagram of OF OUR P REST, signalled by 'Could be', gives a bed instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bed with corner posts is a place where we sleep quietly.

clue.text: Muscle, or numbers primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the numbers piece comes before the other word

parts.note: tens are numbers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between brawn or figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' puts TENS first, though 'or' comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A muscle that tightens or stretches part of the body.

clue.text: Is in favour of trials — or anti?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
tests are trials or experiments

explanation.surface: A question whether someone supports experiments or opposes them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' works with both readings: one who is pro tests favours trials, while one who is anti objects; the joke is that the same letters do both.
explanation.definitionFit: To object to something is to be against it.

clue.text: Capital match ? Juliet thought not

definitions.meaning: a capital city, that of France
the count her parents chose as a husband, a match Juliet rejected for Romeo

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a big contest is a fine idea; Juliet disagrees.
explanation.walkthrough: In Romeo and Juliet the Capulets arrange for Juliet to marry the County of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital shares its name with the count whom Juliet's parents wanted her to wed.

clue.text: This work should give you a rise

definitions.text: This work should give you a rise

parts.words: This work should give you a rise
parts.note: a rise reads as a pay increase for effort, but here it is a slope climbed by toiling

explanation.surface: A promise that this job will earn a salary increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, laborious toil is described as going up a slope, and a rise is an upward slope.

clue.text: Jones proclaims his 3

definitions.meaning: the first name of the architect Jones
3 down is a way in, and someone announcing his own arrival might say the three words making up these letters

explanation.surface: Someone named Jones announces his arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words it is what you say as you go in; and it is the first name of Jones the architect of the Banqueting House.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the architect Jones, and read as three words, an announcement of going in.

clue.text: Wearing second-century clothes?

parts.note: CL is Roman 150, a year in the second century
AD, anno domini, makes the date a year of the Christian era

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is dressed in ancient Roman garments.
explanation.walkthrough: CL AD, the year 150, falls in the second century; the clue's 'clothes' completes the sense of being dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed or covered, having clothing on.

clue.text: These, naturally, many grow out of

definitions.text: These, naturally, many grow out of

parts.words: These, naturally, many grow out of
parts.note: naturally hints at plants, which grow from the underground parts that anchor them; people also grow out of their origins

explanation.surface: A remark that most people naturally outgrow certain habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grow out of' suggests outgrowing a phase; in the plant world it is literal growth from the base.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants grow from the parts beneath the soil, and figuratively people grow from their origins.

clue.text: Wild rose can we find in for instance a byway?

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance

indicators.note: we find in says the next piece is located inside another

parts.note: a lane is a byway, a minor road
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A question whether one can come across a wild rose along a country path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb; it is the container TIN, which 'we find in' LANE, after EG.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetbriar, a wild rose with fragrant leaves, is known by this older name.

clue.text: One thing one doesn't expect to be

definitions.text: One thing one doesn't expect to be

parts.words: One thing one doesn't expect to be
parts.note: a state you cannot anticipate, since anticipating it would cancel it

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark about a condition no one plans for.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught off guard by the unexpected cannot be foreseen.

clue.text: Eye-catching devices

parts.note: not attention-grabbing gadgets but fasteners that engage the eyes of a hook-and-eye pair

explanation.surface: A description of gadgets that attract attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Small metal fasteners catch in a loop called an eye on clothing.
